questions.topic: Celiac Disease and Other Malabsorption Syndromes
questions.stemEn: An 18-month-old girl has diarrhea, abdominal distension, and a rash shown as dermatitis herpetiformis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Celiac disease ويشير إلى dermatitis herpetiformis كارتباط جلدي نوعي مع gluten-sensitive enteropathy.
questions.clinicalPearl: Dermatitis herpetiformis should prompt evaluation for celiac disease.

questions.topic: Celiac Disease and Other Malabsorption Syndromes
questions.stemEn: A child with known celiac disease has an intensely itchy and burning vesicular rash in symmetric clusters on the elbows, knees, buttocks, upper back, and shoulders. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Dermatitis herpetiformis. يصفها بطفح papulovesicular شديد الحكة، متناظر، ويميل إلى extensor surfaces مع celiac disease.
questions.clinicalPearl: Symmetric intensely pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces are classic for dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.topic: Celiac Disease and Other Malabsorption Syndromes
questions.stemEn: A child has diarrhea, flatulence, and abdominal discomfort. Which is the most likely cause among the listed choices?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Lactose intolerance، ويذكر أن الأعراض تشمل abdominal pain, bloating, flatulence, nausea وdiarrhea بعد تناول lactose-containing meals.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Glucose-galactose malabsorption عادةً يظهر كإسهال شديد منذ neonatal period؛ المصدر لا يقدم قرينة لصالح isomaltase deficiency.
questions.clinicalPearl: Post-lactose bloating, flatulence and diarrhea support lactase deficiency.

tts.text: A child has diarrhea, flatulence, and abdominal discomfort. Which is the most likely cause among the listed choices? Option A. Lactose intolerance (lactase deficiency). Option B. Glucose-galactose malabsorption. Option C. Isomaltase deficiency.

questions.topic: Celiac Disease and Other Malabsorption Syndromes
questions.stemEn: An infant on formula had gastroenteritis that resolved, but after formula was restarted he developed flatulence and abdominal distension. What advice is selected in the source?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار lactose-free formula في سياق secondary lactose intolerance بعد gastroenteritis، ويربطها بفقد مؤقت للـlactase بعد أذية mucosa.
questions.clinicalPearl: Transient secondary lactase deficiency can follow infectious gastroenteritis.

tts.text: An infant on formula had gastroenteritis that resolved, but after formula was restarted he developed flatulence and abdominal distension. What advice is selected in the source? Option A. Start lactose-free formula.

questions.topic: Celiac Disease and Other Malabsorption Syndromes
questions.stemEn: An infant has had severe diarrhea since birth. Stool studies show an osmotic gap of 40 and pH 6.3. What is the most likely cause?
questions.recalledAnswer: A (most likely in source; B also considered)
questions.explanationAr: المصدر نفسه غير جازم: يقول إن المعطيات يمكن أن تتماشى مع congenital chloride diarrhea أو congenital sodium diarrhea أو tufting enteropathy، وأن stool electrolytes مطلوبة للفصل بينها. اختار A كـmost likely لأن هذا كان الخيار الوحيد الموافق في إحدى نسخ الامتحان.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: لا يمكن استبعاد tufting enteropathy من القيم المذكورة وحدها بحسب نص المصدر نفسه؛ لذلك لم تُحوَّل A إلى verifiedAnswer.
questions.clinicalPearl: Congenital secretory diarrhea needs fecal electrolyte data to distinguish chloride/sodium diarrhea from enteropathies.

tts.text: An infant has had severe diarrhea since birth. Stool studies show an osmotic gap of 40 and pH 6.3. What is the most likely cause? Option A. Congenital chloride diarrhea. Option B. Tufting enteropathy. Option C. Lactase deficiency.
